LKW’s tears can also be understood in the context of what the union had meant to him. He had spent years advocating for Singapore’s merger with Malaysia, and having to withdraw from the union must have been deeply painful, particularly given that many had followed his vision and political conviction.

Whatever his personal emotions were, the historical record suggests that he came to believe separation was the best course for Singapore. In hindsight, that decision proved consequential for both countries.
